transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-06-30
Start: 15:00 PT
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Carlos Mendez (Redwood AE), Priya Shah (Redwood SE), Jordan Lee (Redwood Solutions) -- Rachel Kim (CISO, Aurora Health), Samir Patel (Head of Cloud), Lena Ortiz (IT Security), Gabe Ortiz (DevOps)

Summary (auto): Quick security review focused on SSO/SAML and SCIM provisioning, RBAC patterns, auditing and KMS. Customer wants least-privilege model and evidence for SOC 2, and is deciding between Dedicated and Private deployment for data residency.

Transcript:
[00:00] Carlos Mendez: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call, and we'll dive into SSO and SCIM, and then Priya will take the RBAC + audit logs piece.
[00:09] Rachel Kim: Hi, Rachel here. We're on a pretty tight compliance timeline, we need SOC two evidence for our Q3 attestation, and data residency for some PHI flows.
[00:20] Priya Shah: Great, thanks. We'll cover how Redwood integrates with SAML IdPs, how SCIM provisioning works for groups, and show recommended role mappings for least privilege.
[00:32] Samir Patel: One thing up front - do you support our Okta setup? We do SCIM + groups and we use IdP-driven group claims.
[00:42] Carlos Mendez: Yes, Okta is a primary supported IdP. We also have docs for Azure AD, Ping, etc. We'll send the specific SCIM mapping doc after this.
[00:50] Lena Ortiz: When you say SCIM, is it one-way provisioning or can we do deprovisioning too? Last thing we want is stale accounts.
[01:00] Priya Shah: SCIM is full two-way provisioning from the IdP side - create, update, deactivate. The usual caveat: deprovisioning behavior can be configured, soft delete vs hard delete, and we recommend a 30-day soft-delete window for compliance teams.
[01:15] Gabe Ortiz: How are roles mapped? We have product roles and team roles and we want least privilege.
[01:21] Jordan Lee: Typically we recommend mapping IdP groups to Redwood roles; create narrowly-scoped roles like read-only, analyst, infra-admin. Then use resource-level entitlements - e.g., limit access to specific projects/environments.
[01:33] Rachel Kim: Can you show an example?
[01:35] Priya Shah: Sure - example mapping: Okta group "redwood-analysts" -> Redwood role "analytics_readonly"; group "redwood-devops" -> "infra_admin" with session MFA required. We'll attach a sample CSV and JSON mapping.
[01:50] Samir Patel: Any support for SCIM group sync filters? We only want to sync production groups, not all internal groups.
[01:58] Priya Shah: Yep, you can scope by attribute or group prefix. We often suggest a naming convention and filter on that prefix.
[02:06] Rachel Kim: Audit logs - what do you capture, and how long can we retain them? We need immutable audit trails for at least 12 months.
[02:15] Priya Shah: Redwood's audit logs capture auth events (SSO logins), SCIM provisioning events, role changes, API keys created, model/version deployments, and admin actions. Retention is configurable; hosted tier defaults to 90 days, Dedicated and Private have options for longer retention - we can push to your SIEM via syslog/Kafka/CloudWatch and retain for 12+ months on your side.
[02:36] Gabe Ortiz: Is the log format structured? JSON? Any schema?
[02:40] Priya Shah: Yes, logs are JSON with fields like timestamp, actor_id, action, target_resource, request_id, request_payload (redacted), outcome. We'll send sample payloads.
[02:52] Samir Patel: Encryption - at rest and in transit? KMS?
[02:55] Carlos Mendez: All data is encrypted in transit with TLS 1.2/1.3. At rest, hosted uses our managed KMS; Dedicated and Private support customer-managed keys via AWS KMS/HSM integrations. We can support bring-your-own-key (BYOK) flows for on-prem.
[03:12] Lena Ortiz: For the BYOK flow, do you support key rotation and do you require access to the key material?
[03:18] Priya Shah: We never see plaintext key material. Rotation is supported through KMS; you rotate keys in your KMS and update the key ARN in Redwood config. We'll document the process and required IAM permissions.
[03:28] Rachel Kim: Data residency - we have a requirement that certain PHI never leaves our VPC or a specific region. Do you offer Private deployments?
[03:36] Carlos Mendez: Yes. Redwood Private is our VPC/on-prem option for regulated workloads. It runs in your VPC and can be configured to keep KV caches and logs in-region only. For absolute in-house processing, we have an on-prem package, though that requires additional ops work.
[03:50] Samir Patel: Performance tradeoffs if we go Private vs Hosted?
[03:53] Jordan Lee: Minor latency differences depending on network topology, but we can often match performance with Dedicated GPU pools in your region. The bigger tradeoff is ops responsibility and patching cadence for on-prem.
[04:05] Rachel Kim: SOC 2 - what artifacts or controls do you provide for us to map?
[04:09] Carlos Mendez: We provide a SOC 2 Type II report, policy docs, access control matrices, and evidence packages: user access lists, change management records, and encryption architecture diagrams. We'll provide a redacted report and a SOC 2 checklist for auditors.
[04:23] Lena Ortiz: Are admin actions and who-approved recorded in audit logs? We need change approvals for role escalations.
[04:29] Priya Shah: Yes, role changes include approver metadata when done through the console workflow. If you require approval gates, we recommend integrating with your ticketing system - we can add a webhook for approvals.
[04:40] Gabe Ortiz: About RBAC least-privilege - do you support temporary elevation or JIT (just-in-time) access?
[04:46] Jordan Lee: We have time-bound role assignments and token TTLs. JIT workflows are possible via API calls combined with your approval system; we can help design a flow for temporary escalation.
[04:58] Samir Patel: For SCIM, how do you handle email changes or username collisions?
[05:03] Priya Shah: SCIM maps users by immutable IdP ID; email changes are updates, collisions typically get flagged and require manual resolution, we can set auto-merge rules but usually customers want a manual review.
[05:14] Rachel Kim: Any gotchas in SAML metadata? We use signed assertions and want to enforce audience restriction.
[05:20] Priya Shah: Signed assertions and audience checking are supported. We recommend enforcing both. We'll send the exact metadata fields Redwood requires and sample ADFS/Okta config snippets.
[05:32] Carlos Mendez: Quick note on permissions in Redwood: service tokens are scoped by route and model; avoid using full-scope tokens for production. Use per-environment tokens and RBAC to restrict who can create service tokens.
[05:45] Samir Patel: Can audit logs show which model generated a given response for traceability?
[05:49] Priya Shah: Yes, logs include model_id, version_id, request_id and token counts. We strip prompt content by default for hosted, but you can opt-in for full payload capture in Dedicated/Private with proper controls.
[06:02] Rachel Kim: What about data retention and deletion for prompts/inputs? PHI must be deletable on request.
[06:08] Priya Shah: We support on-demand deletion and provide an API to remove customer data keys; Dedicated and Private give you full control. For hosted, we have deletion windows and will produce proof of deletion for your compliance team.
[06:20] Lena Ortiz: For our auditors, can you provide a sample of the audit export?
[06:24] Priya Shah: Yes, we'll include a sample JSON and a export playbook that shows how to pull logs for a date range.
[06:30] Carlos Mendez: Let's talk timeline - what's your target for pilot and go/no-go?
[06:35] Rachel Kim: Ideally pilot SCIM + RBAC in two weeks, finalize deployment model by end of July.
[06:41] Carlos Mendez: We'll aim to send docs within 48 hours, and schedule a 30-min SCIM test early next week.
[06:47] Samir Patel: One more - legal asked if Redwood supports contractual clauses for encryption at rest and subprocessor lists.
[06:53] Carlos Mendez: Yes, subprocessor list is in our standard Data Processing Addendum (DPA) and we can negotiate certain contract language. For encryption clauses, we provide KMS integration specifics.
[07:03] Rachel Kim: Great. Any concerns or open items we should note?
[07:06] Priya Shah: The main open items: sample IdP metadata from you, final decision on Dedicated vs Private, retention policy target, and SOC 2 artifacts request.
[07:16] Carlos Mendez: Ok we'll recap next steps in an email. Thanks everyone.

End of transcript.

Notes: transcription includes occasional mis-hearings; product names may appear slightly different in the transcript (e.g., "KV cash" transcribed instead of "KV cache").
